blocks.tex: Coherence requires the circumcenter of each consecutive vertex triple to lie in its open vertex cone. The moderate-arc identities below imply this geometric condition.

blocks.label: def:circumcenter_r2
blocks.title: circumcenter of a plane triple
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, discrete circle of curvature $\rho(P)$, p.~2.}
  For $p, q, r \in \mathbb{C}$ with $u = q - p$, $w = r - p$, set
  \[
    \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,p\,q\,r
      \;=\; p + \frac{\mathrm{i}\,\bigl(|w|^2 u - |u|^2 w\bigr)}
                     {2\,\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w},
  \]
  where $\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w = \mathrm{Im}(\overline{u}\,w)$ is the
  in-tree cross product (\cref{def:cross_r2}). A total function; its
  characterizing properties hold under the non-collinearity guard
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,u\,w \ne 0$. (Center of Dahlberg's discrete circle of
  curvature $\rho(P)$ through the triple.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.circumcenterR2
lean.code:
noncomputable def circumcenterR2 (p q r : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  p + Complex.I * ((normSq (r - p) : ℝ) * (q - p) - (normSq (q - p) : ℝ) * (r - p))
      / (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ))

blocks.label: lem:cross_r2_im_conj_mul
blocks.title: the cross product is the imaginary part of the Hermitian product

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.crossR2_eq_im_conj_mul
lean.code:
lemma crossR2_eq_im_conj_mul (A B C : ℂ) :
    crossR2 A B C = ((starRingEnd ℂ) (B - A) * (C - A)).im := by
  simp only [crossR2, Complex.mul_im, Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im]
  ring

blocks.tex:
Expand both sides in real components; the in-tree definition of
  $\mathrm{crossR2}$ is $u_x w_y - u_y w_x$, which is exactly
  $\mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)$.

blocks.label: lem:circumcenter_dot
blocks.title: perpendicular-bisector identities
blocks.body:
Let $c = \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,p\,q\,r$ and suppose
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,(q-p)\,(r-p) \ne 0$. Then
  \[
    \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\overline{(q-p)}\,(c - p)\bigr) = \tfrac12\,|q-p|^2,
    \qquad
    \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\overline{(r-p)}\,(c - p)\bigr) = \tfrac12\,|r-p|^2 .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub
lean.code:
lemma re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub {p q r : ℂ} (h : crossR2 p q r ≠ 0) :
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (q - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (q - p) / 2 ∧
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) (r - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (r - p) / 2 := by
  have hζ : circumcenterR2 p q r - p
      = (Complex.I * ((normSq (r - p) : ℝ) * (q - p) - (normSq (q - p) : ℝ) * (r - p)))
          / (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ)) := by
    rw [circumcenterR2]; ring
  have hden : (2 * (crossR2 p q r : ℂ)) = ((2 * crossR2 p q r : ℝ) : ℂ) := by push_cast; ring
  have hne : (2 * crossR2 p q r : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0; exact h (by linarith)
  constructor <;>
  · rw [hζ, hden, mul_div_assoc', Complex.div_ofReal_re]
    rw [div_eq_div_iff hne two_ne_zero]
    simp only [Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im, Complex.conj_re, Complex.conj_im,
      Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im, Complex.ofReal_re,
      Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.normSq_apply, crossR2]
    ring

blocks.tex:
Write $\zeta = c - p = \mathrm{i}(|w|^2 u - |u|^2 w)/(2\delta)$ with
  $\delta = \mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)$. Then
  $\mathrm{Re}(\bar u \zeta)
    = \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\mathrm{i}(|w|^2 |u|^2 - |u|^2 \bar u w)\bigr)/(2\delta)
    = |u|^2\,\mathrm{Im}(\bar u w)/(2\delta) = |u|^2/2$,
  using $\mathrm{Re}(\mathrm{i}z) = -\mathrm{Im}(z)$ and
  $\mathrm{Im}(|w|^2|u|^2) = 0$; symmetrically for $w$ (with
  $\mathrm{Im}(\bar w u) = -\delta$). Pure algebra in $\mathbb{C}$.

blocks.label: lem:circumcenter_equidist
blocks.title: the circumcenter is equidistant
blocks.body: Under the same guard, $|c - p| = |c - q| = |c - r|$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.circumcenterR2_equidist
lean.code:
lemma circumcenterR2_equidist {p q r : ℂ} (h : crossR2 p q r ≠ 0) :
    dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) q = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p ∧
      dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) r = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := re_conj_circumcenterR2_sub h
  have key : ∀ x : ℂ,
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) (x - p) * (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)).re = normSq (x - p) / 2 →
        dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) x = dist (circumcenterR2 p q r) p := by
    intro x hx
    have hxp : circumcenterR2 p q r - x = (circumcenterR2 p q r - p) - (x - p) := by ring
    have hsq : normSq (circumcenterR2 p q r - x) = normSq (circumcenterR2 p q r - p) := by
      rw [hxp, normSq_sub' _ _, hx]; ring
    rw [dist_eq_norm, dist_eq_norm,
      ← Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg (circumcenterR2 p q r - x)),
      ← Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg (circumcenterR2 p q r - p)),
      ← Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq, ← Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq, hsq]
  exact ⟨key q h1, key r h2⟩

/-! ## Vertex sectors and local regularity -/

blocks.tex:
$|c - q|^2 = |(c-p) - u|^2 = |c-p|^2 - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(\bar u (c-p)) + |u|^2
  = |c-p|^2$ by \cref{lem:circumcenter_dot}; same for $r$.

blocks.label: def:vertex_sector
blocks.title: vertex sector
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, sector $\mathcal{A}(P)$, p.~2.}
  For a cyclic vertex map $v : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{C}$ and $i \in \ZMod n$,
  \[
    \mathrm{vertexSector}\,v\,i \;=\;
    \bigl\{\, v_i + s\,(v_{i-1} - v_i) + t\,(v_{i+1} - v_i)
      \;:\; s, t \ge 0 \,\bigr\}
  \]
  --- the closed convex cone at $v_i$ spanned by the two incident edge
  directions. (For a non-reflex vertex, interior angle $< \pi$, this is
  exactly Dahlberg's closed convex sector $\mathcal{A}$; every vertex of a
  positively-turning moderate-arc development is non-reflex. The $k = 0$
  half-plane convention is out of scope per the chapter preamble.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.vertexSector

blocks.label: def:locally_regular
blocks.title: locally regular polygon
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, Definition 1, p.~3.}
  $\mathrm{LocallyRegularR2}\,v$ holds when for every $i \in \ZMod n$ the
  consecutive triple is non-collinear,
  $\mathrm{crossR2}\,(v_{i-1} - v_i)\,(v_{i+1} - v_i) \ne 0$, and
  \[
    \mathrm{circumcenterR2}\,v_i\,v_{i-1}\,v_{i+1}
      \;\in\; \mathrm{vertexSector}\,v\,i .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.LocallyRegularR2
lean.code:
def LocallyRegularR2 (v : ZMod n → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ZMod n, crossR2 (v i) (v (i - 1)) (v (i + 1)) ≠ 0 ∧
    circumcenterR2 (v i) (v (i - 1)) (v (i + 1)) ∈ vertexSector v i

/-! ## Dahlberg's Proposition 1 (non-reflex case) -/

blocks.title: Plateau-aware local extrema and the DFV bridge

blocks.label: def:plateau_local_max
blocks.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
blocks.body:
\textit{Source: Dahlberg, $I(f,P)/\hat I$ vocabulary, p.~2.}
  For $f : \ZMod n \to \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \ZMod n$:
  $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMax}\,f\,i$ holds when there are an
  $\mathbb{N}$-lift $a$ and a length $k < n$ with
  $i \in \{a, a+1, \dots, a+k\}$ (as residues), $f$ constant $= f(i)$ on
  that run, and $f(a - 1) < f(i)$, $f(a + k + 1) < f(i)$.
  $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMin}$ is the same with reversed inequalities
  (its own block below). Two
  plateau extrema are \emph{distinct} when their defining runs are disjoint.
  (Existential form of Dahlberg's definition: a run with strict drops at
  both extended ends is automatically the maximal plateau $I(f,i)$, since a
  constant run cannot cross a strict drop; so this is equivalent to his
  ``$f(Q) < f(P)$ on $\hat I \setminus I$'' and avoids formalizing the
  maximality of $I(f,P)$.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsPlateauLocalMax
lean.code:
def IsPlateauLocalMax (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ a k : ℕ, k < n ∧ PlateauMaxRun f a k ∧ ∃ m ≤ k, i = ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n)

blocks.label: def:plateau_local_min
blocks.title: plateau local minimum
blocks.body:
As in \cref{def:plateau_local_max} with the strict inequalities reversed:
  $f(a-1) > f(i)$ and $f(a+k+1) > f(i)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsPlateauLocalMin
lean.code:
def IsPlateauLocalMin (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ a k : ℕ, k < n ∧ PlateauMinRun f a k ∧ ∃ m ≤ k, i = ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n)

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.label: def:plateau_max_run
blocks.title: explicit plateau maximum run
blocks.body:
$\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$ packages the run-level data of
  \cref{def:plateau_local_max}: $f$ constant on the residues of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$, and $f(a-1) < f(a)$, $f(a+k+1) < f(a)$. (The bound
  $k < n$ is \emph{not} part of the predicate --- it is carried alongside it
  by every consumer, e.g.\ \cref{def:plateau_local_max} and
  \cref{cor:dfv_plateau_extrema_window}; it is in fact forced, since a run of
  length $\ge n-1$ would wrap and contradict the strict drop at $a-1$. The bridge
  theorem's conclusion is phrased with these explicit runs, which carry the
  disjointness data two abstract point-form extrema would lose.)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun
lean.code:
def PlateauMaxRun (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (a k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m ≤ k, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n) = f (a : ZMod n)) ∧
    f ((a : ZMod n) - 1) < f (a : ZMod n) ∧
    f ((a + k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) < f (a : ZMod n)

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.label: def:plateau_min_run
blocks.title: explicit plateau minimum run
blocks.body: As \cref{def:plateau_max_run} with the strict inequalities reversed.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMinRun
lean.code:
def PlateauMinRun (f : ZMod n → ℝ) (a k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m ≤ k, f ((a + m : ℕ) : ZMod n) = f (a : ZMod n)) ∧
    f (a : ZMod n) < f ((a : ZMod n) - 1) ∧
    f (a : ZMod n) < f ((a + k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)

blocks.label: lem:plateau_max_run_isMax
blocks.title: a maximum run is a plateau local maximum
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{PlateauMaxRun}\,f\,a\,k$ then every residue of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMax}\,f$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMaxRun.isPlateauLocalMax
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMaxRun.isPlateauLocalMax {f : ZMod n → ℝ} {a k : ℕ} (hk : k < n)
    (h : PlateauMaxRun f a k) : IsPlateauLocalMax f (a : ZMod n) :=
  ⟨a, k, hk, h, 0, Nat.zero_le k, by rw [Nat.add_zero]⟩

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.tex:
The run itself is the witnessing run of \cref{def:plateau_local_max};
  constancy transports the plateau value to the chosen point.

blocks.label: lem:plateau_min_run_isMin
blocks.title: a minimum run is a plateau local minimum
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{PlateauMinRun}\,f\,a\,k$ then every residue of
  $\{a, \dots, a+k\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{IsPlateauLocalMin}\,f$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.PlateauMinRun.isPlateauLocalMin
lean.code:
lemma PlateauMinRun.isPlateauLocalMin {f : ZMod n → ℝ} {a k : ℕ} (hk : k < n)
    (h : PlateauMinRun f a k) : IsPlateauLocalMin f (a : ZMod n) :=
  ⟨a, k, hk, h, 0, Nat.zero_le k, by rw [Nat.add_zero]⟩

/-! ## The DFV window yields Dahlberg's conclusion class -/

blocks.label: thm:dfv_plateau_bridge
blocks.title: the DFV window yields Dahlberg's conclusion class
blocks.body:
If $\mathrm{DFV}(\kappa; c)$ (\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex}), then
  $\kappa$ has two distinct plateau local maxima and two distinct plateau
  local minima (in the sense of \cref{def:plateau_local_max,def:plateau_local_min}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.dfv_plateau_extrema
lean.code:
theorem dfv_plateau_extrema {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ : ℕ}
    (h12 : i₁ < i₂) (h23 : i₂ < i₃) (h34 : i₃ < i₄) (h41 : i₄ < i₁ + n)
    (hκ1 : c < κ ((i₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) (hκ2 : κ ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c)
    (hκ3 : c < κ ((i₃ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) (hκ4 : κ ((i₄ : ℕ) : ZMod n) < c) :
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMaxRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMaxRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) ∧
    (∃ a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ, k₁ < n ∧ k₂ < n ∧
        PlateauMinRun κ a₁ k₁ ∧ PlateauMinRun κ a₂ k₂ ∧
        ∀ m₁, m₁ ≤ k₁ → ∀ m₂, m₂ ≤ k₂ →
          ((a₁ + m₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) ≠ ((a₂ + m₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n)) := by
  -- the two period-shifted window values
  have e1 : ((i₁ + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = ((i₁ : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
    push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]; ring
  have e2 : ((i₂ + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = ((i₂ : ℕ) : ZMod n) := by
    push_cast [ZMod.natCast_self]; ring
  constructor
  · -- MAXIMA: arcs (i₂, i₄) through i₃ and (i₄, i₂+n) through i₁+n
    obtain ⟨a, b, hA1, hA2, hA3, hAc, hAL, hAR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h23.le h34.le
        (lt_trans hκ2 hκ3) (lt_trans hκ4 hκ3)
    obtain ⟨a', b', hB1, hB2, hB3, hBc, hBL, hBR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h41.le
        (show i₁ + n ≤ i₂ + n by omega)
        (by simp only [e1]; exact lt_trans hκ4 hκ1)
        (by simp only [e1, e2]; exact lt_trans hκ2 hκ1)
    have hk1 : b - a < n := by omega
    have hk2 : b' - a' < n := by omega
    refine ⟨a, b - a, a', b' - a', hk1, hk2,
      plateauMaxRun_of_natRun (by omega) hA2 hAc hAL hAR,
      plateauMaxRun_of_natRun (by omega) hB2 hBc hBL hBR, ?_⟩
    intro m₁ hm₁ m₂ hm₂
    exact natCast_zmod_ne (by omega) (by omega)
  · -- MINIMA: arcs (i₁, i₃) through i₂ and (i₃, i₁+n) through i₄
    obtain ⟨a, b, hA1, hA2, hA3, hAc, hAL, hAR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => -κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h12.le h23.le
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ2 hκ1)
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ2 hκ3)
    obtain ⟨a', b', hB1, hB2, hB3, hBc, hBL, hBR⟩ :=
      exists_max_run (fun m : ℕ => -κ ((m : ℕ) : ZMod n)) h34.le
        (show i₄ ≤ i₁ + n by omega)
        (by simpa using lt_trans hκ4 hκ3)
        (by simp only [e1]; simpa using lt_trans hκ4 hκ1)
    have hk1 : b - a < n := by omega
    have hk2 : b' - a' < n := by omega
    refine ⟨a, b - a, a', b' - a', hk1, hk2,
      plateauMinRun_of_natRun (by omega) hA2
        (fun x h1 h2 => neg_inj.1 (hAc x h1 h2)) (by simpa using hAL)
        (by simpa using hAR),
      plateauMinRun_of_natRun (by omega) hB2
        (fun x h1 h2 => neg_inj.1 (hBc x h1 h2)) (by simpa using hBL)
        (by simpa using hBR), ?_⟩
    intro m₁ hm₁ m₂ hm₂
    exact natCast_zmod_ne (by omega) (by omega)

deps.label: lem:plateau_min_run_isMin

deps.title: plateau local extrema on a cyclic profile
deps.label: def:plateau_local_max

blocks.tex:
Let $i_1 < i_2 < i_3 < i_4 < i_1 + n$ be the window, with
  $\kappa_{i_2}, \kappa_{i_4} < c < \kappa_{i_1}, \kappa_{i_3}$. Consider
  the closed cyclic arc $B_1 = [i_2, i_4]$ (through $i_3$) and
  $B_2 = [i_4, i_2 + n]$ (through $i_1 + n$, i.e.\ through $i_1$). On the
  finite arc $B_1$ pick $j$ attaining $\max_{B_1} \kappa \;(> c$, witnessed
  by $i_3)$. The maximal constant run of $\kappa$ through $j$ cannot reach
  either endpoint $i_2, i_4$ (their values are $< c <$ the run value), so
  the run together with its two extension neighbours stays inside $B_1$;
  the extension neighbours are non-attaining points of the arc adjacent to
  a maximal run, hence have value strictly below the max. That run is a
  plateau local max. The same on $B_2$ (witness $i_1$) produces a second
  one; the two runs live in the disjoint open arcs
  $(i_2, i_4)$ and $(i_4, i_2 + n)$, so they are distinct. For minima run
  the mirrored argument on the arcs $[i_1, i_3]$ (through $i_2$) and
  $[i_3, i_1 + n]$ (through $i_4$) with $\min$ in place of $\max$. Finite
  combinatorics on $\mathbb{N}$-lifts throughout; no geometry.
